whoWeAre.title: Who We Are
whoWeAre.description:
We are Vision Jeunesse Nouvelle—a community-driven organization rooted in faith, resilience, and a deep belief in the potential of youth.

Founded in 2002 by the Brothers of Christian Instruction (FIC), we are more than just an NGO—we are a movement committed to transforming lives and shaping a more peaceful, empowered, and creative generation.
whoWeAre.mission: To develop talents and capacities that promote human dignity, peace, and sustainable development—one youth at a time.
whoWeAre.vision: A renewed, dynamic, and productive population in good physical, moral, and spiritual health, building a brighter future for all.
whoWeAre.different:
We reach across borders—serving both Rwandan youth and those in refugee communities.

We build peace through dialogue, arts, sports, and youth-led action.

We invest in skills, self-reliance, and long-term transformation, not just short-term aid.

We believe talent is not a luxury—it's a calling. We develop it from a very young age.

From Gisenyi to Mahama, from peace camps to business trainings, we walk beside the youth—never ahead, never behind—always together.

We are VJN.
A voice for the voiceless. A home for the hopeful. A platform for purpose.

intro.description: Our Health Program is dedicated to promoting holistic well-being among youth and communities. We focus on preventive education, access to health services, and fostering healthy lifestyles to ensure a vibrant and resilient future.

details.title: Program Details
details.background: The Health program was established by Vision Jeunesse Nouvelle in 2023. The idea to start this program came after identifying various health challenges faced by youth who lacked access to sufficient information and support services.
details.recreation: VJN also recognized that many youth participating in recreational activities could face accidents requiring basic first aid. Additionally, many sports activities at VJN require medical staff to treat athletes.
details.youngMothers: The program also addresses the needs of young mothers who lack sufficient knowledge about reproductive health and childcare. While various health services are provided to youth, additional services are needed to continue supporting youth health.
details.partners: VJN has helped youth access various health services through training funded by Imbuto Foundation in the Baho neza, Mountain Movers, and Door to Door Campaign projects. The organization also supports young mothers and their parents through savings and credit groups with MISEREOR and Imbuto Foundation.

objectives.title: Program Objectives
objectives.main: To improve the well-being of partners through various trainings, help them access sufficient health information, and provide various services to minimize the effects of poor health.
objectives.specific1: Provide training to enhance youth knowledge about health-related matters.
objectives.specific2: Help youth access basic health services and provide counseling to help them maintain good health.
objectives.specific3: Advocate for youth in various institutions.
objectives.specific4: Connect parents and children from families with conflicts related to young mothers.
objectives.specific5: Help youth reduce the effects of poor health.

peace.title: Peace Building Program
peace.subtitle: Building Peace Through Youth Empowerment
peace.description: Our program addresses the root causes of conflict by equipping youth with tools for conflict resolution and promoting a culture of peace in Rwanda and the Great Lakes region.

intro.description: Our Peace Building Program is dedicated to fostering social cohesion and reconciliation among youth. We promote dialogue, conflict resolution, and inter-community understanding to build a more peaceful and inclusive society.

details.title: Program Details
details.history: The Peace Building program was established by Vision Jeunesse Nouvelle in 2012, recognizing the persistent conflicts in the Great Lakes region and the need for youth empowerment to foster peace. Initially, efforts focused on resolving family conflicts and addressing trauma among youth in the Western Province.
details.expansion: Over time, the program expanded to include training in peace education, conflict resolution, and leadership skills. VJN has partnered with various organizations, including AEGIS TRUST, NEVER AGAIN RWANDA, and HROC (Healing and Rebuilding Our Communities), to implement its peace initiatives.
details.impact: The program has successfully trained over 1,000 young people and community leaders in peace building techniques, enabling them to mediate conflicts and promote reconciliation in their communities.

objectives.title: Program Objectives
objectives.main: To empower youth with conflict resolution skills and promote a culture of peace in the Great Lakes region.
objectives.specific1: Equip youth with knowledge and skills to resolve conflicts peacefully.
objectives.specific2: Promote reconciliation and social cohesion among communities.
objectives.specific3: Advocate for youth participation in peace-building processes.
objectives.specific4: Provide psychosocial support to victims of conflict and trauma.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Find answers to common questions about our organization and programs.

q1.title: How can I volunteer with VJN?
q1.answer: You can apply to volunteer through our Careers page. We welcome both local and international volunteers with various skills and backgrounds.

q2.title: How is my donation used?
q2.answer: Your donations directly support our programs for youth empowerment, including education initiatives, entrepreneurship training, and peace-building activities.

q3.title: Can my organization partner with VJN?
q3.answer: Yes, we welcome partnerships with organizations that share our mission. Please contact us with your partnership proposal, and our team will get back to you.

q4.title: Where do your programs operate?
q4.answer: Our programs operate primarily in the Rubavu District, with our headquarters in Gisenyi. We collaborate with partners across Rwanda to extend our reach.

olivier.quote: The agricultural training and support from VJN helped me establish my farming enterprise. I've learned modern farming techniques and business management skills.

abdoulah.quote: VJN's technical training program equipped me with the skills to start my electronics repair business. Now I provide essential services to my community while building a sustainable enterprise.
